body:
## Symptom

`tests/test_table_structure.py` fails two tests on a warm workstation cache:

```
FAILED ...::TestTableStructure::test_declared_columns_present[CotedIvoire/cluster_features]
FAILED ...::TestFeatureSanity::test_feature_is_sane[CotedIvoire/cluster_features]
AssertionError: CotedIvoire/cluster_features: declared column 'Latitude'
                not found in ['Region', 'Rural', 't', 'v']
```

Found during the Ghana audit (PR #673); reproduced on `master` (`ad4b9c1f`) in an isolated worktree with the import asserted to come from the worktree rather than the `.pth`-pinned main checkout, so it is not branch-specific.

## It is not a code defect — and that is the interesting part

The test reads a **cached parquet**. Ours (mtime 2026-07-21) has columns `['Region','Rural']`. A **cold rebuild of the same table** yields `['Region','Rural','Latitude','Longitude']` (Latitude 34.8% null). So the code is right and the cache is wrong.

## Why the content hash did not catch it

This is the part worth fixing. The cached parquet carries an `lsms_cache_hash` that grades it **fresh**, yet its content is degraded — a required column is simply missing.

The likely path is the **GH #515 optional-sub-df fallback**. `CotedIvoire/_/data_scheme.yml` documents that `Latitude`/`Longitude` come from a `df_geo` merge on `Menage/grappe_gps_CIV2018.dta`, and that until 2026-07-13 that file carried **no `.dvc` sidecar**, so in a clean checkout it was absent, the #515 fallback swallowed the `PathMissingError`, and Lat/Lon dropped out silently. If a build runs while that file cannot be fetched, the parquet is written **without** the column but **with** a perfectly valid hash.

The consequence generalises beyond CotedIvoire:

> A build degraded by a transient fetch failure is cached as though it were a good build, and **no amount of hash-checking will ever re-derive it**. The hash covers the *inputs the build declared*, not *what the build actually managed to read*.

`Country._assert_built_required_columns` and the `grab_data` `KeyError` guard both live on the **build** path, so they fire when the degraded build happens — but once the bad parquet is written, every subsequent warm read sails past them.

## Possible directions

- Record in the parquet metadata whether any `dfs:` sub-df was **dropped** during the build (the #515 fallback already knows), and treat a parquet built with a drop as not-fresh — or at least warn loudly on read.
- Fold "set of columns actually produced" into the cache hash, so a parquet missing a declared-required column cannot grade fresh.
- Refuse to *write* a parquet that is missing a column declared required and not marked `optional` — i.e. fail the build rather than cache the damage. (Closest to the repo's existing posture; `_assert_built_required_columns` already raises on the country-level twin.)

## Related

- GH #515 (the optional-sub-df fallback this rides on)
- The v0.8.0 content-hash design in `SkunkWorks/dvc_object_management.org` — this is a gap in the "*Limitations*" list, alongside the dynamically-built-paths and `assume_cache_fresh` cases already recorded in `CLAUDE.md`.
- Practical note: it also means **CI green on a cold cache does not imply green on a developer's warm cache**, and vice versa. Both CotedIvoire failures above are invisible to a cold run.
title: A degraded build caches as fresh: parquet missing a required column still carries a valid content hash
